purpose: Canonical formulas and calculation explanations for the project copilot.

formulas.name: Current Ratio
formulas.plain_english: This measures whether short-term assets can cover short-term obligations.

formulas.name: Quick Ratio
formulas.formula: quick_ratio = (cash_and_equivalents + accounts_receivable) / current_liabilities; fallback quick_ratio = (current_assets - inventory) / current_liabilities
formulas.plain_english: This is a tighter liquidity check than current ratio. It uses receivables directly when available, or excludes inventory from current assets as a fallback.

formulas.name: Cash Ratio
formulas.plain_english: This checks how much short-term liability coverage exists in cash.

formulas.name: Debt To Equity
formulas.plain_english: This measures leverage against book equity.

formulas.name: Debt To EBITDA
formulas.plain_english: This estimates how many years of EBITDA would be needed to cover debt, ignoring growth and cash leakage.

formulas.name: Interest Coverage
formulas.plain_english: This measures how comfortably operating profit covers interest expense.

formulas.name: PCA First Principal Component
formulas.plain_english: PCA compresses several market stress components into one main market factor. If enough component history exists, the first principal component becomes the combined stress signal.

formulas.name: PCA Market Stress Index
formulas.plain_english: The first principal component is rescaled to a 0-100 stress index so the dashboard and models can read it as low-to-high stress.

formulas.name: Jet Crack Spread
formulas.plain_english: EIA jet fuel is stored in dollars per gallon, so it is multiplied by 42 to convert to dollars per barrel before subtracting crude. A wider spread means aviation fuel is expensive relative to crude.

formulas.name: Merton Distance To Default
formulas.plain_english: Distance to default estimates how far assets are from the debt barrier after accounting for volatility and time.

formulas.name: Merton Structural PD
formulas.plain_english: Lower distance to default produces a higher default probability.

formulas.name: ML Proxy PD
formulas.plain_english: The ML side uses ratios and market features as a data-driven cross-check. It is trained on free-source proxy distress labels, not internal bank default data.

formulas.name: Final PD Blend
formulas.formula: final_pd = clip((structural_weight * structural_pd + ml_weight * ml_pd) * sqrt(financial_trend_pd_multiplier)) when financial history is available; otherwise the multiplier is 1.0
formulas.plain_english: The final default probability combines the structural model and the ML model. If the user supplied multiple years or quarters, deteriorating or improving financial history can apply a capped multiplier.

formulas.name: Financial Trend Overlay
formulas.formula: trend_risk_score = capped sum of revenue, margin, debt, leverage, coverage, liquidity, cash, and fuel-cost trend pressures minus improvement offsets
formulas.plain_english: The overlay is neutral with less than two periods. With enough history, worsening trends can slightly raise PD and LGD, while improving trends can slightly reduce PD.

formulas.name: LGD Blend
formulas.formula: predicted_lgd = clip(0.65 * business_lgd + 0.35 * trained_lgd, 0.01, 0.99) when trained LGD is available
formulas.plain_english: LGD starts with collateral-aware business logic and then uses the trained artifact as a severity cross-check.

formulas.name: Business EAD
formulas.plain_english: EAD estimates the exposure that could be outstanding at default, capped by the relevant credit limit when available.

formulas.name: EAD Blend
formulas.formula: exposure_at_default = 0.70 * business_ead + 0.30 * trained_ead, capped by logical_limit when applicable
formulas.plain_english: The final EAD combines deterministic exposure logic with the calibrated EAD artifact.

formulas.name: Expected Loss
formulas.plain_english: Expected loss turns default likelihood, severity, and exposure into a currency amount.

formulas.name: Risk Grade Mapping
formulas.plain_english: The project maps numeric PD to an internal proxy grade. This is not an external rating agency grade.

formulas.name: Recommended Credit Limit
formulas.plain_english: The credit engine starts from requested limit, approved limit, or EAD, then applies risk haircuts.

formulas.name: Recommended Tenor
formulas.plain_english: Riskier names get shorter tenors to control receivable build-up.

formulas.name: Recommended Security
formulas.plain_english: The engine asks for stronger security when PD, grade, or policy score is weaker.

formulas.name: Approval Status
formulas.plain_english: The final decision label is a policy output. The copilot should explain it, not create a new one.
